For every $\epsilon ,\kappa >0$ there is $\alpha (\epsilon ,\kappa )$ such that if $x,y\in M_\epsilon $ and $R(x)d(x,y)^2>\alpha $, then for every $z$ either $R(x)d(z,x)^2<\alpha $, or $R(y)d(z,y)^2<\alpha $, or $R(z)d(z,\overline{xy})^2<\alpha $ and $z\notin M_\epsilon $.
Proof

Cylindrical cross-sections force a round cylindrical limit, contradicting the neck status; rescaling at the nearest point makes $z$ an $\epsilon $-neck center.
